feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. Integration compensation: the weights follow the iteration 5 gradient (x/0.018, clipped), so kp and kd stay at the iteration 5 values (3.5 and 0.5). With more sensors the signal scale is unchanged, so no gain rescaling was needed. Evidence: iteration 5 (422.9) is the best design, with oval finish 95% and slalom line losses 1.85. Iteration 8 showed that widening the outer spread to +/-0.045 m cut slalom line losses to 1.0 but dropped oval finish to 65%, so spread has a cost that density may avoid. Iteration 3 showed that look-ahead at y=0.08 m raised oscillation to 0.36 and cut oval finish to 35%, so the forward offset stays at y=0.07 m. Depending on the next race: if slalom line losses fall below 1.85 with oval finish at or above 90% and oscillation at or under 0.3, keep seven sensors and try the outer-spread test again at this density. If oscillation rises above 0.32 while max_error does not move, the extra sensors add steering noise, so revert to five sensors at iteration 5 values. If s-bend max_error stays near 0.06 m with few line losses, the limit is turn authority, not sensing.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.85 and oval finish stays at or above 90%, keep the seven-sensor layout and try the outer sensors at x = +/-0.045 m with 0.0075 m pitch (seven sensors, 16 mm footprint). Iteration 8 showed the wider span cut slalom line losses to 1.0, and seven sensors at finer pitch may keep the oval finish that the five-sensor +/-0.045 m test lost.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.32 on any track while max_error does not move, revert to five sensors at y=0.07 m with x = -0.036, -0.018, 0, 0.018, 0.036 and 16 mm footprints. Iteration 3 showed that extra sensors at a forward offset raised oscillation and cut the oval finish rate.
Keep wheel_radius at 0.040 m and mass at 0.5 kg. Iteration 9 (radius 0.045 m) fell to 389.9 with oval finish 80%, and iteration 6 (0.4 kg) lowered s-bend progress to 0.59.
